title: Change Windows Are a Design Choice
stat: 69 percent of platform teams now automate at least some release steps, a 19-point jump from last year
source: A published industry survey of platform engineers this year
topic_claim: the practice of treating change windows as fixed is now the default answer
story_examples: One deploy pipeline merged eight services and paged no one when the second one failed.
Another team approved a change in a ticket and shipped the opposite change an hour later.
A third rebuilt the same dashboard three times because the source query lived in three places.
thesis: Change windows work when the review question becomes a design question: which decisions stay human, which get automated, and who verifies both. The pipeline's choices need to be on the record. Expose the decisions, and the boundary moves by design
design_moves: log what got filtered before you looked
counter: Teams lean on the fixed window when they configure their pipelines. The framing reads as prudence, and prudence calms stakeholders more than it protects the review
definition: Decision surface is the set of calls an automated pipeline makes before a reviewer reads a word
gap_stat_a: 61 percent of engineers trust automation to find patterns
gap_stat_b: only 47.6 percent trust it to turn patterns into recommendations
takeaway: Build for traceability: keep the review human, expose the decisions, log every filter.
question_tail: Where in your pipeline does a decision still happen that you never see?
person_context: I run change windows for a platform team
